question: All executive actions of the Government of a state shall be expressed to be taken in the name of _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __Governor.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

Governor:

__
 
• The Governor’s appointment, his powers and everything related to the office of Governor has been discussed under Article 153 to Article 162 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The role of the Governor is quite similar to that of the President of India.
 
• The Governor performs the same duties as of President, but for the State.
 
• Governor stands as the executive head of a State and the working remains the same as of the office of the President of India.
 
• All the executive action of a state government shall be exercised by order in the name of the Governor.
 
• Under the Constitution of India, the governing machinery is the same as that of the Central Government.
 
• It is stated that the Governor has a dual role.
 
 
• He is the constitutional head of the state, bound by the advice of his council of ministers.
 
• He functions as a vital link between the Union Government and the State Government.
 
 
 
• The term of the governor's office is normally 5 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to Article 164 in the Indian Constitution, Governor appoints Chief Minister.
 
• However, the Governor cannot appoint any random person as the Chief Minister but has to follow a provision.
 
• A leader of the party that has got the majority share of votes in the assembly elections, is appointed as the Chief Minister of the state. 

 
• 
 
 
• Article 75:- The PM shall be appointed by the President and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the PM.

 
 
• The total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the COM, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
 
• A minister who is not a member of the Parliament (either house) for any period of six consecutive months shall cease to be a minister.
 
 
 
• Article 75 clearly states that the COM is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
 
 
• This means that all the ministers own joint responsibility to the Lok Sabha for all their acts of omission and commission.
 
 
 
• Article 75 also contains the principle of individual responsibility.
 
 
• It states that the ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, which means that the President can remove a minister even at a time when the COM enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
 
• However, the President removes a minister only on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
 
 
• The council of Ministers comes into existence after the Ministers have taken the oath to their respective offices.
